name: L.I.F.T.
aliases: Luminal Improvement Following Prostatic Tissue Approximation
question: Does the prostatic urethral lift improve lower urinary tract symptoms from BPH more than sham cystoscopy in men with 30 to 80 cc prostates and no obstructive median lobe?

design.blinding: patient and outcome assessor blinded through 3 months

arms.label: sham rigid cystoscopy with simulated lift sounds

design.population: Men aged 50 years or older with AUASI of 13 or higher, Qmax of 12 mL/s or less and prostate volume of 30 to 80 cc, without an obstructive median lobe.
design.description: Multicenter, sham-controlled, blinded randomized device trial
design.locator: Abstract; Can J Urol 2017 PDF pp3-4 (journal pp8804-8805); Can J Urol 2015 PDF pp2-3, Table 1

verdictNote: Symptom score and flow improved versus sham at 3 months; the randomized comparison ended at 3 months.
takeaway: The prostatic urethral lift (UroLift) reduced the AUA symptom index more than sham at 3 months (11.1 versus 5.9 points) in men 50 or older with BPH-related LUTS and 30 to 80 cc prostates without a median lobe; no de novo sustained sexual dysfunction occurred.

reports.label: Randomized sham-controlled report
reports.citation: Roehrborn CG, Gange SN, Shore ND, et al. The prostatic urethral lift for the treatment of lower urinary tract symptoms associated with prostate enlargement due to benign prostatic hyperplasia: the L.I.F.T. study. *J Urol.* 2013;190(6):2161-2167. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2013.05.116
reports.followUp: 3-month blinded comparison; lift arm followed to 12 months

results.measure: 3-month change in AUA symptom index (reduction from baseline), intention to treat
results.note: Mean change from baseline (SD 7.67 and 7.66). The abstract states that the primary endpoint was met; the difference in change and its interval are those quoted in the AUA 2026 BPH guideline.
results.locator: Abstract; AUA 2026 BPH guideline PDF p39

results.measure: 3-month change in IPSS quality-of-life item (reduction from baseline)
results.note: Means 2.2 (SD 1.8) versus 1.0 (SD 1.5), as reported in the five-year paper's account of the randomized comparison; difference and interval as quoted in the AUA 2026 guideline.
results.locator: Can J Urol 2017 PDF p4 (journal p8805); AUA 2026 BPH guideline PDF p39

results.measure: 3-month change in peak urinary flow rate
results.note: Means 4.28 (SD 5.16) and 1.98 (SD 4.88); the difference is calculated from the two means. Central over-read of uroflow tracings with the 2-second rule.
results.locator: Can J Urol 2017 PDF pp3-4 (journal pp8804-8805); AUA 2026 BPH guideline PDF p39

results.measure: AUASI in the lift arm over 12 months (no sham comparison after 3 months)

values.exp: 22.1 at baseline; 18.0 at 2 weeks; 11.0 at 3 months; 11.1 at 12 months

results.note: P value for change from baseline in the lift arm.
results.locator: Abstract

results.measure: Increase in Qmax in the lift arm

values.exp: +4.4 mL/s at 3 months; +4.0 mL/s at 12 months

results.note: P value for change from baseline in the lift arm.
results.locator: Abstract

harms.label: De novo erectile or ejaculatory dysfunction
harms.note: Sustained de novo events were a secondary safety endpoint; mean sexual function measures did not differ between groups at 3 months (Can J Urol 2017 PDF p4).

harms.label: Subjects with a related adverse event, months 0-3
harms.locator: J Urol 2013 PDF p6, Table 4 (journal p2166)
harms.note: 203 related events in the lift arm, adjudicated by an independent committee; sham arm 20/66 (30.3%) with 26 related events. Most frequent in the lift arm: dysuria 48 (34.3%), hematuria 36 (25.7%), pelvic pain or discomfort 25 (17.9%) and urgency 10 (7.1%), typically mild to moderate and resolved within 2 weeks.

harms.label: Catheterization for failed voiding trial
harms.note: Forty lift men were catheterized routinely as standard of care; of the remaining 100, 32 (32%) required a catheter after the voiding trial. Mean duration of catheterization 0.9 days.

delivery.label: Anesthesia
delivery.note: In North America all procedures but one (99.4%) used local anesthesia (Can J Urol 2017 PDF p3, journal p8804).

delivery.label: Implants placed
delivery.value: Mean 4.9 (range 2 to 11) in the 2013 report; four implants in 42% and six or fewer in 85% in the five-year report
delivery.locator: J Urol 2013 PDF p4 (journal p2164); Can J Urol 2017 PDF pp3-4 (journal pp8804-8805)

delivery.label: Return to preoperative activity
delivery.locator: Can J Urol 2017 PDF p4 (journal p8805)

reports.label: Sexual function analysis
reports.citation: McVary KT, Gange SN, Shore ND, et al. Treatment of LUTS secondary to BPH while preserving sexual function: randomized controlled study of prostatic urethral lift. *J Sex Med.* 2014;11(1):279-287. doi:10.1111/jsm.12333
reports.followUp: 3-month blinded comparison; lift arm to 12 months

results.measure: 3-month erectile (SHIM) and ejaculatory (MSHQ-EjD) scores, lift versus sham
results.note: Scores did not differ from sham at 3 months; men with baseline SHIM below 5 were censored from the primary sexual function analysis.
results.locator: Abstract

results.endpoint: SHIM and MSHQ-EjD in the lift arm
results.measure: 12-month scores versus baseline in the lift arm
results.note: Modestly improved and statistically different from baseline at 1 year. Ejaculatory bother score improved most (40% over baseline).
results.locator: Abstract

results.endpoint: SHIM in severe baseline erectile dysfunction
results.measure: 12-month SHIM versus baseline in men entering with severe erectile dysfunction
results.note: Secondary stratified analysis by baseline erectile dysfunction severity.
results.locator: Abstract
